title: Defensive, failure-tolerant classes
idea: Defensive programming makes each class reject bad input at its edge and stay valid; resilient design keeps the system useful when a dependency fails.
points: Validate arguments in constructors and public methods, and fail fast.
Copy mutable inputs in, and hand out unmodifiable views.
Keep invariants safe: `final` fields and no setters, so state stays valid.
Retry short-lived failures a few times, then fall back to a safe answer.

steps.caption: A call arrives with a blank name.
The guard rejects it at once. No half-built object ever exists.
A valid call arrives with a name and a tag list.
The guards pass, and the constructor copies the list in.
The object starts valid. Callers cannot change its list from outside.
Later the code needs a remote rate. The call times out.
It tries again, up to three attempts in all. Each one fails.
Instead of crashing, it returns a cached rate and the request completes.

code.title: Guard clauses and copies
code.caption: `Profile` checks its inputs and copies the list, so no caller can make it invalid.

walk.text: Guard clauses: refuse `null` and blank names before any field is set.
`List.copyOf` takes a private, unmodifiable copy of the caller's list.
The caller changes its own list afterwards; the profile does not see it.
The getter returns the unmodifiable list, so writes through it fail.
Both bad names are rejected with a clear message.

code.title: Retry, then fall back
code.caption: A fake remote service fails a set number of times. `Retry` tries a few times, then uses the fallback. Real code waits between attempts (backoff); the demo skips it to stay deterministic.

walk.text: A stand-in for a network call: it times out a fixed number of times.
Catch only `RemoteTimeoutException`. `Supplier` cannot throw checked exceptions, so it is unchecked here.
After the last attempt, return the fallback instead of failing the caller.
The first service recovers on attempt three; the second never does.

pitfalls: Do not catch `Exception` and ignore it; log it or rethrow with context.
Retry only calls that are safe to repeat, and wait longer between attempts (backoff).
Cap retries; unlimited retries turn one outage into a flood of calls.

quiz.q: Using `Profile` above, what does this print?
quiz.why: The constructor stored `List.copyOf(tags)`, a separate copy. Adding to the caller's list later does not reach the profile.

takeaway: Reject bad input early, protect your state, plan for failing dependencies.
